experiment: class-pair accuracy work (strategy C): class weighting and 6/7 specialist
question: Can recall on the weak classes 6/7 (and 0/3) be improved enough to raise the geometric-mean score without losing robustness under distribution shift?
protocol: Fit on the seed-42 80k train split, tune on the 5k calibration rows only, score once on the untouched 15k check rows; the seed-123 split repeats the comparison; the 400-row demo (drawn like the evaluation data) is the final gate. Demo labels were never used for fitting or tuning.

baseline_reproduction.note: Slightly above the recorded value because the offset search adds a 0.0625 step.

candidates.name: ungated 6/7 specialist (binary HGB on the same 231 features, argmax override)
candidates.verdict: rejected: flips 457 decisions (210 fixed, 185 broke); trades class 6 recall for class 7

candidates.name: confidence-gated 6/7 specialist (tau=0.5, pair-margin<=0.25, tuned on calibration rows)
candidates.demo_verdict: neutral: demo score 2.565 and accuracy 77.25%, identical to the shipped package
candidates.verdict: rejected: no gain on the shifted demo, and the gate thresholds cannot be honestly re-tuned for the final refit (its calibration rows were seen in training) without holding out fresh rows

candidates.name: class-weighted main fit, weights x2 on classes 6/7
candidates.demo_verdict: class-6 recall falls 0.44 -> 0.34 on demo; its term drops 0.35 -> 0.10
candidates.verdict: rejected: helps in-distribution (+0.15/+0.23 across two splits) but clearly hurts on the evaluation-like distribution; upweighting train-file class frequencies is exactly the shift the organizers warn about

candidates.name: class weights x2 on 0/3 as well

conclusion: Both mechanisms improve the in-distribution check score but fail or stay neutral on the demo distribution. The shipped package (pruned-extractor balanced_core_200) remains the best known configuration. In-distribution gains did not transfer to the shifted evaluation-like data; consistent with the organizers' warning that the evaluation data differs in noise, ranges and class balance.
